answer: In this PoA design, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow, while provable equivocation is correlated across identities through shared timing, messages, and signing patterns. When k identities coordinate, penalties scale as O(k^2); once detected, recursive slashing and asymmetric depreciation impose an exponential multiplier on aggregate capital loss. Thus opal, vine, and ocean accounts cannot cheaply diversify risk, making sybil control costlier than honest participation.
